h: Complete Rectification and the Two Messiahs

p: פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ בַּמִּסְפָּר תְּשִׁיעִי מִסֵּפֶר בְּרֵאשִׁית,
— This parashah is ninth in order in the Book of Genesis,
הַמְכֻוָּון נֶגֶד מִדַּת יְסוֹד
— which corresponds directly to the sefirotic attribute of Yesod (the ninth sefirah),
שֶׁהוּא תִּיקּוּן פְּגַם הַבְּרִית.
— which is the rectification of the blemish of the covenant.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי בַּתּוֹרָה נִמְצְאוּ גַּ"ן (53) סְדָרִים
— And this is because within the Torah are found 53 weekly portions,
לְבַד פָּרָשַׁת "וְזֹאת הַבְּרָכָה" שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִקְרָא בְּשַׁבָּת רַק בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
— excluding Parashat Vezot HaBerakhah which is not read on a regular Sabbath but on the Festival of Simchat Torah,
וְשָׁם מַתְחִיל שׁוֹרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ.
— and there commences the root of the Oral Torah of Moses our teacher.
וְהַגַּ"ן סְדָרִים:
— And these 53 portions contain mystical meaning:
הַנּוּ"ן מְרַמֵּז עַל חֲמִשִּׁים שַׁעֲרֵי בִינָה,
— the Nun (50) alludes to the fifty gates of Understanding (Binah),
שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הֵ"א רִאשׁוֹנָה כַּיָּדוּעַ
— which corresponds to the first letter Hei of the Tetragrammaton as is known,
שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מֵהֵ"א כָּלוּל בְּעֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת;
— wherein each of the 5 sub-levels is factored across ten sefirot (5 × 10 = 50);
וְהַגִּימֶ"ל מְרַמֵּז עַל תְּלָת חֲלָלִין דְּגוּלְגַּלְתָּא
— and the Gimel (3) alludes to the three cranial chambers of the Supernal Skull
שֶׁמִּבְּחִינַת חָכְמָה מוֹחָא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָ"ב נְתִיבוֹת חָכְמָה.
— which derive from Chokhmah-Mocha possessing the 32 Paths of Wisdom.
וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז סִיּוּם הַתּוֹרָה בְּלָמֶ"ד
— And to this hints the conclusion of the Torah with the letter Lamed (לְעֵינֵי כָל יִשְׂרָאֵל)
נֶגֶד תְּלָת חֲלָלִין שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד כָּלוּל בְּעֶשֶׂר (30),
— facing the three chambers each comprised of ten (3 × 10 = 30),
וּבֵי"ת מִ"בְּרֵאשִׁית"
— and the opening letter Beit (2) of Bereishit
נֶגֶד שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַהַשְׁפָּעָה מִלְּעֵילָא מִמִּדַּת חָכְמָה (וְיַחַד לֵ"ב נְתִיבוֹת).
— facing the twin root of influx from Above from Chokhmah (together totaling the 32 Paths).
וְהַיְינוּ כְּנֶגֶד שְׁנֵי הַדִּבְּרוֹת: "אָנֹכִי" וְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה" שֶׁמִּפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה שְׁמַעֲנוּם,
— And that is facing the two initial commandments: “I am” and “You shall have no other,” which we heard directly from the mouth of the Almighty,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּשְׁפַּע הֶאָרָה דִּלְעֵילָא לִהְיוֹת נִקְבָּע בְּלִבֵּנוּ בְּחִינַת "אָנֹכִי" וְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה",
— signifying that a celestial illumination was channeled to be engraved in our hearts as “I am” and “You shall not have”,
דְּאִיתָא (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה א, טו):
— for it is stated (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:15):
שֶׁבְּדִבּוּר "אָנֹכִי" נִתְקַע תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה בְּלִבָּם
— that through the utterance “I am,” Torah study was planted firmly in their heart,
וּבְדִבּוּר "לֹא יִהְיֶה" נֶעֱקַר יֵצֶר הָרָע מִלִּבָּם.
— and through the utterance “You shall have no other,” the evil inclination was uprooted from their heart.

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2:4: “Rabbi Yehuda says: When Israel heard ‘I am Hashem your God,’ Torah learning became fixed in their hearts: they learned and did not forget. When they asked Moses to be the intermediary, they again learned and forgot… Rabbi Nechemya says: When Israel heard ‘You shall have no other gods,’ the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts. When they asked Moses to be the intermediary, the inclination immediately returned to its place. They asked that He reveal Himself again; Moses said: This is for the future, as it is written, ‘I shall remove the heart of stone from your flesh.’” The passage is numbered 1:15 in the edition cited by Rav Tzadok; the linked edition places it under Song of Songs 1:2.

p: וּבְכָל סִדְרָה תְּשִׁיעִית מֵחוּמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה
— And in every ninth parashah across the five books of the Torah
יֵשׁ בּוֹ הִתְגַּלּוּת מִדַּת צַדִּיק לְפִי אוֹתָהּ בְּחִינָה שֶׁל הֵ"א רִאשׁוֹנָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
— there resides the manifestation of the attribute of Tzaddik according to that dimension of the higher Hei as noted.
לָכֵן נִמְצָא בָּהּ תִּיקּוּן עַל פְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
— Therefore there is found within it rectification for the blemish of the covenant,
מַה שֶּׁנִּרְאֶה לָעַיִן שֶׁחָלִילָה נִתְקַלְקֵל הַכֹּל וְאֵין תִּקְוָה חָלִילָה,
— even in that which appears to human sight as though all were ruined and there were no hope, Heaven forbid,
וְדַיְיקָא בָּזֶה נַעֲשָׂה שְׁלֵימוּת הַתִּיקּוּן.
— and precisely in this situation complete rectification is achieved.
כַּאֲשֶׁר הָיָה בְּרֵאשִׁית הַפְּגָם בְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
— Just as occurred at the original inception of the blemish with Adam the First,
שֶׁכָּל הַמֵּאָה וּשְׁלוֹשִׁים שָׁנָה שֶׁנִּרְאֶה לָעַיִן שֶׁהוֹלִיד וְכוּלֵי דַּחֲזָא לְאוֹנְסֵיהּ
— where throughout all those 130 years wherein it appeared to the eye that he generated spirits, etc., seeing his involuntary impurity
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב עֵירוּבִין יח:),
— (as written in Eruvin 18b),
וְאָז דַּיְיקָא הָיָה תִּיקּוּנוֹ,
— yet specifically right then did his repentance and rectification transpire,
וּכְמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם: שֶׁיָּשַׁב בְּתַעֲנִית וְהֶעֱלָה זַרְזֵי תְּאֵנִים עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ.
— and as they stated there: that he sat in fasting and placed belts of rough fig twigs upon his flesh.
הֲגַם שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁנִּשְׁאַר הַמִּיתָה,
— Although in this physical world, as long as physical mortality remains,
לֹא יְתוּקַּן לְגַמְרֵי הַחֵטְא הַזֶּה לִהְיוֹת זְדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשִׂים כִּזְכִיּוֹת
— this sin cannot be completely transformed into merits
עַד לֶעָתִיד כְּשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה אוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ.
— until the ultimate future when the light of the Messiah will be revealed.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Takanas HaShavin 10:13: “So is the way of Hashem in the creation of the world: first darkness and then light. So they said in Bereishit Rabbah that He was creating worlds and destroying them; these are the worlds of tohu, until the world of tikkun came forth, as is known. So it is in everything. All the incarnations of the Messiah that have already been in the world are a likeness of ‘creating worlds and destroying them,’ and precisely through those destructions came the building of the world of tikkun, by raising the lights of the broken vessels, as is known. The Messiah is the one who comes to rectify the root of the evil in Creation. This is the sin of the generation of the Flood and the sin of Er and Onan: where the light of holiness is aroused, there arises opposite it an intensified power of evil, for ‘one opposite the other.’ It is called ‘evil in the eyes of Hashem’: so of Onan it says, ‘and it was evil in the eyes of Hashem,’ and so it says of King David, ‘and the thing was evil in the eyes of Hashem,’ and so he said of himself, ‘and I have done what is evil in Your eyes.’”

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 18b: “The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita: Rabbi Meir would say: Adam the first man was very pious. When he saw that death was imposed as a punishment because of him, he observed a fast for a hundred thirty years, and he separated from his wife for a hundred thirty years, and wore belts (zarzei) of fig leaves on his body as his only garment for a hundred thirty years. If so, how did he father demons into the world?”

h: The Emergence of the Two Messiahs

p: וְהוּא הָעִנְיָן הַנִּזְכָּר בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ
— And this is the very dynamic described in this parashah,
שֶׁהָיוּ עֲסוּקִים בְּשַׂקָּם וְתַעֲנִיתָם לְאַחַר מַעֲשֶׂה זוֹ
— wherein they sat occupied in their sackcloth and fasting following that terrible deed
שֶׁהָיָה נִרְאֶה לְעֵינֵיהֶם שֶׁפָּגְמוּ בְּמִדַּת יְסוֹד מַה שֶּׁאֵין לוֹ תִּיקּוּן וְחָלִילָה אָפַס תִּקְוָה.
— where it appeared to their eyes that they had damaged the attribute of Yesod beyond remedy and Heaven forbid all hope was gone.
כִּי גַּם יוֹסֵף בְּעַצְמוֹ פָּגַם בְּהוֹצָאַת דִּבָּה וְלָשׁוֹן הָרָע גַּם כֵּן כִּפְגַם הַבְּרִית שֶׁנִּקְרָא "רָע",
— For even Joseph himself had blemished through bringing evil report and slander which parallels the covenantal defect termed “evil”,
כִּי בְּרִית הַלָּשׁוֹן וּבְרִית הַמָּעוֹר מְכֻוָּונִים כַּיָּדוּעַ.
— for the covenant of the tongue and the covenant of circumcision correspond directly, as is known.
וּלְאַחַר שֶׁרָאָה מַה שֶּׁנּוֹלַד מִזֶּה שֶׁמְּכָרוּ אוֹתוֹ לְמִצְרַיִם,
— And after he saw what sprouted from this—that they sold him into Egypt,
אָז הִתְמַרְמֵר בְּנַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁהוּא גָּרַם לָזֶה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁפָּגַם בְּמִדַּת יְסוֹד.
— he then was bitterly broken in his soul that he had caused this by impairing the attribute of Yesod.
וּמַה גַּם הַשְּׁבָטִים בְּעַצְמָם,
— And how much more so the brothers themselves,
שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי הִתְמַרְמְרוּ מְאֹד שֶׁהֵמָּה הָיוּ בַּעֲלֵי מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁמָּכְרוּ אֶת יוֹסֵף
— who certainly were exceedingly aggrieved that they were the perpetrators who sold Joseph
שֶׁהָיָה מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם לְמִצְרַיִם,
— who was the chariot for Tzaddik, Foundation of the World, down into Egypt,
וְהָיָה נִדְמֶה לָהֶם שֶׁחַס וְשָׁלוֹם אָפַס תִּקְוָה.
— and it appeared to them that Heaven forbid all hope was lost.
וְעַל יְדֵי מַעֲשֶׂה זוֹ דַּיְיקָא הָיָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בּוֹרֵא אוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ,
— Yet through this very crisis specifically, the Holy One was creating the light of the Messiah,
וְהַיְינוּ שְׁלֵימוּת הַתִּיקּוּן שֶׁל חַיֵּי עוֹלָם שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד,
— which is the absolute perfection of eternal life embodied in Mashiach ben David,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סֻכָּה נב.):
— as they taught in Sukkah (52a):
מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד שֶׁעָתִיד לְהִגָּלוֹת וְכוּלֵי,
— Mashiach ben David who is destined to be revealed, etc.,
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁרָאָה מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף שֶׁנֶּהֱרַג,
— and once he saw Mashiach ben Yosef slain in battle,
אָמַר לוֹ: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, אֵינִי מְבַקֵּשׁ מִמְּךָ אֶלָּא חַיִּים;
— he said to Him: Master of the Universe, I ask of You nothing other than life;
אָמַר לוֹ: חַיִּים? עַד שֶׁלֹּא אָמַרְתָּ כְּבָר הִתְנַבֵּא עָלֶיךָ דָּוִד אָבִיךָ:
— He said to him: Life? Before you spoke your father David already prophesied concerning you:
"חַיִּים שָׁאַל מִמְּךָ נָתַתָּה לּוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים כא, ה).
— “He asked life of You, and You gave it to him” (Psalms 21:5).
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי מִדַּת מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף הוּא בְּחִינַת צַדִּיק,
— And this is because the spiritual mode of Mashiach ben Yosef is the rung of Tzaddik,
לִהְיוֹת נִזְהָר בְּכָל מַעֲשָׂיו בְּלֹא שְׁגִיאָה וּמִכְשׁוֹל,
— to be flawlessly guarded in all his actions without error or stumbling,
וּבֶאֱמֶת אֵין בָּזֶה קִיּוּם לִכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— yet in truth there is no lasting survival for the collective of Israel under that standard,
וְלָכֵן יִהְיֶה נֶהֱרָג.
— and therefore he is destined to be slain.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהִבִּיטוּ אֵלַי אֵת אֲשֶׁר דָּקָרוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (זְכַרְיָה יב, י),
— And this is what is written: “And they shall look unto Me whom they have pierced, etc.” (Zechariah 12:10),
שֶׁזֶּה נֶאֱמַר עַל מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף שֶׁנֶּהֱרַג
— which is expounded as referring to Mashiach ben Yosef who is slain
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם בְּסֻכָּה),
— (as written there in Sukkah),
וְהַיְינוּ אֲשֶׁר דָּקְרוּ הֵם בְּעַצְמָם בְּסִבַּת הַכְּלָל שֶׁאֵין יְכוֹלִים לַעֲמוֹד עַל פִּי בְּחִינָתוֹ.
— meaning whom they pierced through the spiritual shortcoming of the collective who cannot endure according to his exacting standard.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Erev Yom Kippur 2:1: “Judah corresponds to Yesod. For although Joseph is the chariot for the attribute of Yesod, we find that Mashiach ben Yosef will be slain, as it says in Sukkah 52a, while of Mashiach ben David it is written, ‘He asked life of You; You gave it to him.’ The attribute of Joseph was mastery over his inclination, and he did not blemish at all; what befell him was repaired through the Ten Martyrs, as is known. But here Judah comes to repair the blemish of Adam the First after the ruin. In Judah the ruin began, with Er and Onan, and afterwards with King David, of whom it is written as though he had blemished in this; yet in truth our Sages said that David was not fit for that deed, and it happened only to teach repentance to the individual, as our Sages said (Avodah Zarah 5a) on the verse ‘the utterance of the man raised on high’: that he raised up the yoke of repentance. Mashiach ben David will be the individual who repented, whose repentance will bring repentance into the heart of all Israel; of this it says (Yoma 86b) that on account of one individual who repented the whole world is forgiven. Then the entire blemish of Adam the First will be repaired: the bodily pleasure the serpent brought in when he cast filth into her.”

It grounds the difference in Joseph’s standard of never having blemished, against Judah’s line, which repairs after the ruin through teshuvah. It adds that what befell Joseph himself was repaired through the Ten Martyrs.

p: וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה טָעוּת הַשְּׁבָטִים,
— And it can be suggested that this was the very mistake of the brothers,
מֵחֲמַת שֶׁרָאוּ זֹאת שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה קִיּוּם עַל פִּי בְּחִינָתוֹ,
— because they perceived that there could be no enduring existence according to his perfectionist path,
רַק דַּיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי אוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד,
— save specifically through the compassionate illumination of Mashiach ben David,
וְהוּא בְּחִינַת חַיֵּי עוֹלָם שֶׁכָּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים נִתְקָנִים.
— which embodies eternal life wherein all actions are ultimately rectified through repentance.
וְזֶה נִתְגַּלָּה בִּגְמַר הַמַּעֲשֶׂה עַל יְדֵי תּוֹלְדוֹת פֶּרֶץ וְזֶרַח
— And this was unveiled at the conclusion of the episode through the births of Peretz and Zerach
שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת אוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ,
— which represents the light of the Messiah,
וְדַיְיקָא מִגִּלְגּוּל עֵר וְאוֹנָן שֶׁהֵם פָּגְמוּ בָּזֶה בְּפֹעַל,
— and specifically from the reincarnation of Er and Onan who had actually blemished in this deed,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "רַע בְּעֵינֵי ה'" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לח, ז),
— as it is stated: “evil in the sight of Hashem” (Genesis 38:7),
שֶׁהוּא עַל הַפּוֹגֵם בַּבְּרִית שֶׁהוּא נִקְרָא "רָע" – הֵיפֶךְ שֶׁל "טוֹב",
— which refers to one who blemishes the covenant who is titled “evil”—the absolute opposite of “good”,
וְאֵין טוֹב אֶלָּא צַדִּיק,
— and there is no “good” other than the Tzaddik,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אִמְרוּ צַדִּיק כִּי טוֹב" (חֲגִיגָה יב.).
— as it is stated: “Say of the righteous that he is good” (Chagigah 12a).
וְזֶה נִצְמַח מֵאֲכִילַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע
— And this blemish sprouted from the eating of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil
שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה הָעִרְבּוּב טוֹב וָרָע.
— whereby good and evil became intermingled.
וְכֵן כְּשֶׁאֵירַע לְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אוֹתוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה
— And likewise when that incident happened to King David, peace be upon him,
אָמַר: "וְהָרַע בְּעֵינֶיךָ עָשִׂיתִי" (תְּהִלִּים נא, ו),
— he confessed: “and I have done that which is evil in Your sight” (Psalms 51:6),
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׂוֹנֵא זִמָּה,
— because the Holy One despises illicit immorality,
וּכִבְיָכוֹל כְּאִלּוּ אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל וּמוֹאֵס לִרְאוֹת הָרָע בְּעֵינָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ.
— and as it were, He abhors and refuses to gaze upon evil with His holy eyes.

p: וּכְנִרְאֶה מֵהַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה לִפְגָם זֶה,
— And while it appears from the holy Zohar that repentance is ineffective for this sin,
וּבֶאֱמֶת יָדוּעַ שֶׁאֵין דָּבָר עוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה
— yet in truth it is established that nothing can stand in the way of repentance,
וְעַל הַכֹּל יֵשׁ תִּיקּוּן,
— and for everything there is rectification,
אִם רַק נוֹתֵן אֶל לִבּוֹ זֹאת וְיִתְמַרְמֵר עַל גּוֹדֶל הַפְּגָם
— if one only takes this to heart and is bitterly broken over the severity of the flaw
לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁמָר בָּזֶה מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא,
— resolving to be strictly guarded in this from here onward,
מִמֵּילָא יוּכַל לַחֲסוֹת בַּה' שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִתְקָן הַכֹּל.
— then automatically he can take refuge in Hashem so that all is rectified.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ בְּרֶמֶז הַמִּדְרַשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ:
— And as we noted regarding the hint of Midrash Rabbah at the opening of this parashah:
"וְהַחֹסֶה בִי יִנְחַל אֶרֶץ" – זֶה יַעֲקֹב,
— “but he who takes refuge in Me shall inherit the land”—this refers to Jacob,
שֶׁהוּא כְּרֶמֶז הַפָּסוּק: "וְלֹא יֶאְשְׁמוּ כָּל הַחֹסִים בּוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים לד, כג),
— which mirrors the verse: “and none of those who take refuge in Him shall be desolate” (Psalms 34:23),
שֶׁכָּל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב לֹא יֶאְשָׁמוּ,
— that all the seed of Jacob shall never be desolate,
אַף שֶׁצְּרִיכִין פִּדְיוֹן – "פּוֹדֶה ה' נֶפֶשׁ עֲבָדָיו"
— even though they require redemption: “Hashem redeems the soul of His servants”
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר ד).
— (and this was explained in Discourse 4).

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Takanat HaShavin §15, paragraph 39: “In any event, as everyone has understood the Zohar’s statement that he has no repentance—to refer to the very forgiveness of the sin and its atonement—it is certainly puzzling and strange, and everything they have written about it is strained and remote. … But in accordance with what I wrote above about the penitential disciplines arranged by the Rokeach and the Arizal—that they do not hold up atonement, but serve as a gift, each according to his level—it seems clear to me that the Zohar, too, intends the reconciliation brought by the gift: that a person should be fully accepted, ascending and appearing before God on lofty levels, like a completely righteous guardian of the covenant who never sinned. With transgressions generally, complete repentance from love turns deliberate sins into merits, and through them he shall surely live. After the requisite repentance and the subsequent gift, he again becomes close and a member of the household as before—even more so, since his transgressions also count as mitzvot. It is of this that the Zohar says that, for this transgression, repentance does not suffice to turn it into merits and restore the person completely to his former state, even after all the gifts. … Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai’s attainment and what he revealed to his companions were higher than all the others, as is known from what the holy Zohar says about him and his generation: there would be no generation like it, and such a revelation would not recur until the coming of the Messiah. In keeping with their attainment, they said that repentance for this sin does not enable one to reach so exalted a level; only a perfectly righteous guardian of the covenant who never blemished it can reach that level.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Rav Tzadok here supplies a precise distinction between forgiveness and restored access to the most exalted spiritual intimacy. The Zohar’s severe language concerns the latter; it cannot mean that pardon is unavailable. This explains how the present assurance that repentance can repair the sin coexists with the earlier qualification in this discourse that its complete transformation into merit awaits the revelation of the Messiah. It preserves both claims without weakening either.

p: וְאִיתָא בְּסֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר (סִימָן קצז):
— And it is brought in Sefer HaBahir (section 197):
שֶׁפֶּרֶץ וְזֶרַח מְרַמְּזִים לְחַמָּה וּלְבָנָה:
— that Peretz and Zerach allude to the sun and the moon:
פֶּרֶץ עַל שֵׁם הַלְּבָנָה שֶׁהַלְּבָנָה נִפְרֶצֶת לְעִתִּים,
— Peretz is named after the moon, for the moon is breached (diminished) periodically,
וְזֶרַח אִיקְרֵי עַל שֵׁם הַחַמָּה שֶׁזּוֹרַחַת תָּמִיד כְּעִנְיַן "וְזָרַח הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ" (קֹהֶלֶת א, ה).
— and Zerach is titled after the sun which shines perpetually, as in “The sun also rises” (Ecclesiastes 1:5).
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי זֶרַח הָיָה גִּלְגּוּלוֹ שֶׁל אוֹנָן,
— And this is because Zerach was the reincarnation of Onan,
וּמִפְּנֵי שֶׁבּוֹ נִכְתַּב הַמַּעֲשֶׂה מְפוֹרָשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה יוֹתֵר מִשֶּׁנִּכְתַּב בְּעֵר
— and because regarding Onan the sin is recorded explicitly in the Torah far more than with Er,
שֶׁאֵצֶל עֵר נִכְתַּב רַק בְּרֶמֶז,
— for concerning Er it is written only by subtle hint,
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ שֶׁמַּה שֶּׁנִּכְתַּב בַּתּוֹרָה בְּפֵירוּשׁ מוֹרֶה שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה חֲקוּקָה בַּנֶּפֶשׁ,
— and we have already established that what is explicitly articulated in the Torah shows that it was deeply etched into the soul,
מִמֵּילָא הַפְּגָם שֶׁל אוֹנָן יוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל,
— consequently the blemish of Onan was far more severe,
וּמִמֵּילָא הָיָה נִצְרָךְ תִּיקּוּנוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עַל יְדֵי הֶאָרָה גְּדוֹלָה כִּזְרִיחַת הַחַמָּה.
— and consequently his rectification required an immensely powerful illumination like the radiant shining of the sun.
אָמְנָם בְּעֵר, שֶׁהַפְּגָם נִכְתַּב רַק בְּרֶמֶז,
— However regarding Er, whose sin was recorded only by hint,
נִתְקַן בְּתוֹלְדוֹת פֶּרֶץ שֶׁהוּא דּוּגְמַת הַיָּרֵחַ שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם הַפְּגָם שֶׁלָּהּ,
— he was rectified in the offspring of Peretz who mirrors the moon whose deficiency is restored,
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת אוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד שֶׁחַי וְקַיָּם בְּחַיֵּי עוֹלָם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
— and that is achieved through the light of Mashiach ben David who is alive and enduring in eternal life as mentioned above.
וְעַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת נִתְקָן הַכֹּל,
— And through the sanctity of Shabbat everything is rectified,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קיח:):
— as they stated in the Gemara (Shabbat 118b):
שֶׁכָּל הַמְשַׁמֵּר שַׁבָּת כְּהִלְכָתוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כֶּאֱנוֹשׁ מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ,
— whoever observes Shabbat according to its halakhot, even if he served idolatry like the generation of Enosh, he is forgiven,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "שֹׁמֵר שַׁבָּת מֵחַלְּלוֹ וְשֹׁמֵר יָדוֹ מֵעֲשׂוֹת כָּל רָע" (יְשַׁעְיָה נו, ב) –
— as it is stated: “He that keeps the Sabbath from profaning it (mechalelo), and keeps his hand from doing any evil (ra)” (Isaiah 56:2) –
"רָע" דַּיְיקָא,
— specifically “evil”, denoting covenantal blemish,
וּכְתִיב "מֵחַלְּלוֹ" – מָחוּל לוֹ, כְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם.
— and it is read “mechalelo”—machul lo (he is forgiven), as they expounded there.

paragraphs.text: Sefer HaBahir 197: “Rabbi Amorai sat and expounded: Why did Tamar merit that Peretz and Zerach descend from her? Because her name was Tamar… Why were they called Peretz and Zerach? Peretz was named after the moon, which is diminished at times and will be rebuilt in the future. Zerach was named after the sun, which shines continually in one manner. But Peretz was the firstborn, and the sun is greater than the moon! This is no difficulty: it is written, ‘He put out a hand,’ and afterwards, ‘His brother came out, upon whose hand was the scarlet thread, and he called his name Zerach.’ He ought to have been the firstborn. But the Holy One, rejoicing because He foresaw that Solomon would descend from Peretz and would recite the Song of Songs, turned Zerach back.”
